messages.text:
"The core concept is a hardcore open-world 3D vehicle mechanic and survival simulator. The gameplay loop seamlessly blends high-fidelity mechanical assembly with punishing first-person life simulation.
The player starts in a remote rural area with a completely bare car chassis and a garage full of loose individual parts like pistons, crankshafts, and wiring looms. Every component must be manually installed and fastened using specific tool sizes, where loose bolts lead to mechanical failure and overtightening strips the threads. Beyond assembly, the player must finely tune the engine, including carburetor fuel-air mixtures, valve clearances, and wheel alignment, while parts realistically wear down or catastrophically fail under stress.
To fund this project, the player navigates the open world using secondary vehicles like tractors, mopeds, or trucks to perform odd jobs for local residents, such as hauling firewood or clearing septic tanks. Survival mechanics run parallel to the mechanical simulation, requiring the player to manage shifting meters for hunger, thirst, fatigue, stress, and hygiene, where failure or severe driving accidents result in permadeath. The game features no active hand-holding or guidance, immersing the player in a gritty, high-stakes sandbox of automotive grease, financial struggle, and raw mechanical trial-and-error
"

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a playable browser prototype of the user's hardcore open-world 3D vehicle-mechanic/survival game concept: bare chassis assembly with real torque specs, engine tuning, tractor odd jobs, survival meters, and permadeath.

## Requirements
- Game concept includes: manual part installation with specific tool sizes; loose bolts cause failure and overtightening strips threads; engine tuning (carburetor mixture, valve clearance, timing); parts wear/fail; secondary vehicles (tractor/moped/truck) for jobs like firewood hauling and septic pumping; open-world rural area; survival meters (hunger, thirst, fatigue, stress, hygiene); permadeath; no hand-holding/guidance; gritty high-stakes sandbox.
- Existing repo conventions require mobile/touch support and responsive layouts.

## Decisions
- Built a single-page Three.js (r160, vendored locally) web game titled **HARD START**.
- Two 3D scenes: a detailed garage assembly scene and a procedural low-poly rural driving world, switched with fades.
- 14 installable components with tool/torque specs; torque minigame requires correct wrench size and releasing within the green torque band.
- Parts with no fasteners (gasket, wiring loom) install via "SEAT COMPONENT".
- Engine tuning uses three drag knobs and a synthesized tachometer/audio; quality must reach ≥42 to start, ≥85 for "runs clean".
- Jobs: firewood, septic pump, hay delivery, scrap haul; septic uses a pressure-band minigame.
- Survival and economy are persistent in `localStorage`; death wipes the save (permadeath).
- Used procedural canvas textures and synthesized WebAudio instead of external assets; vendored fonts to avoid CDN dependency.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html`, `styles.css`, and all core modules written.
- Garage scene: room, lighting, props, bare chassis, 14 part meshes, hover markers, camera orbit/focus, install animations, smoke/dust.
- Torque minigame with wrench selection, gauge, loose/stripped outcomes, replacement purchases, re-torque.
- Tuning overlay with tach, knobs, crank/stall/run logic, live engine audio.
- World: terrain, roads, trees, buildings, tractor + trailer, driving physics, collisions, fuel, jobs, job markers, compass, phone, home actions, refuel, tow.
- Survival decay, death screen, title screen, continue/new run, mobile joystick/brake/use/jobs controls.
- Playwright/Chromium installed and local server running; page loads without JS errors (only favicon 404 and PMREM warning).

### Active
- Visual polish pass on garage lighting/materials and composition; latest screenshot shows the title screen only because the click landed before reload/new-run completed (or clicked wrong target), so the new garage props/lighting are not yet visually verified.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Reload and start a new run; capture garage screenshot to verify the new lighting, front-wall windows, parts cart, hazard stripe, and oil stain.
2. Tune brightness/contrast further if the scene is washed out; engine block should read as dark cast iron, not white.
3. Test the full loop: install several parts → torque minigame (success/loose/stripped) → install all 14 → tune/crank → HEAD OUT → drive to sawmill → load firewood → deliver to farm → earn cash.
4. Verify mobile layout and touch controls via resized browser; check compass/job tracker and phone.
5. Check console for runtime errors after interactions, especially `tqStripped`, tuning knobs, job modal, and scene transitions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: DOM shell, all HUD panels/overlays, import map.
- `styles.css`: full industrial UI styling, responsive/mobile rules, gauges/knobs.
- `src/main.js`: renderer, UI wiring, torque/tuning/job/phone logic, scene flow, input, main loop.
- `src/garage.js`: garage environment, chassis/part meshes, camera, picking, markers, animations.
- `src/world.js`: terrain, roads, buildings, tractor physics, jobs, compass data, day/night.
- `src/state.js`: game state, survival/time, parts/tuning, economy, jobs, save/load/death.
- `src/data.js`: part specs, torque/tool requirements, tuning ranges, locations, jobs.
- `src/audio.js`: synthesized engine, ratchet, pump, UI and ambience sounds.
- `src/textures.js`: procedural concrete, metal, wood, road, hazard, oil-stain, sign textures.
- `vendor/three.module.js`: vendored Three.js r160.
- `vendor/fonts/`: vendored Barlow Condensed and IBM Plex Mono woff2 files.
- `screenshots/`: test captures (`title.png`, `garage1-3.png`).

## Important Context
- Local server runs in tmux session `serve` at `http://localhost:3002` (`python3 -m http.server 3002`).
- Playwright CLI works after installing Chromium; launch config uses headed Chromium with Xvfb/SwiftShader, so rendering is CPU software rendering.
- `game` is a singleton exported from `src/state.js`; UI polls state each frame and saves every 20 seconds.
- `game.die()` now wipes the save and `game.save()` refuses to save when mode is `'dead'`.

- Latest screenshot `screenshots/garage3.png` shows only the title screen; the garage after the lighting/prop changes still needs verification.
- No commits have been made; all work is uncommitted in the working tree.

"The core concept is a hardcore open-world 3D vehicle mechanic and survival simulator. The gameplay loop seamlessly blends high-fidelity mechanical assembly with punishing first-person life simulation.
The player starts in a remote rural area with a completely bare car chassis and a garage full of loose individual parts like pistons, crankshafts, and wiring looms. Every component must be manually installed and fastened using specific tool sizes, where loose bolts lead to mechanical failure and overtightening strips the threads. Beyond assembly, the player must finely tune the engine, including carburetor fuel-air mixtures, valve clearances, and wheel alignment, while parts realistically wear down or catastrophically fail under stress.
To fund this project, the player navigates the open world using secondary vehicles like tractors, mopeds, or trucks to perform odd jobs for local residents, such as hauling firewood or clearing septic tanks. Survival mechanics run parallel to the mechanical simulation, requiring the player to manage shifting meters for hunger, thirst, fatigue, stress, and hygiene, where failure or severe driving accidents result in permadeath. The game features no active hand-holding or guidance, immersing the player in a gritty, high-stakes sandbox of automotive grease, financial struggle, and raw mechanical trial-and-error
